topic: keep the header row visible while scrolling in Excel
core_question: How do I make the top row stay on screen as I scroll down a spreadsheet?
answer_summary: On the View tab, choose Freeze Panes > Freeze Top Row so the header stays visible while scrolling through the rest of the sheet.
persona: anxious and rambling; writing in full careful sentences

messages.content: I'm working with this spreadsheet and every time I scroll down, the column headers at the top disappear and I lose track of what data is in each column. It's making me crazy trying to remember what column B and C are supposed to be. How can I keep those headers visible?

That's a really common frustration when you're working with large datasets, isn't it? When you're scrolling through your data, what part of the spreadsheet would you most want to stay in place while the rest moves? Do you think Excel has a feature designed specifically for this problem?

It sounds like you're doing a lot of unnecessary scrolling, which definitely slows you down—have you ever noticed any menu or button in Excel that mentions keeping rows or columns locked in place? What menu options do you see when you click on View at the top?
